fixes.what: The plan stage validates the work order's schema (line 569) and the split's criteria (line 577) but never runs check-forbidden.mjs — grep -c 'check-forbidden' over the file returns 0, while sdlc-implement.yml:130 and sdlc-root-cause.yml:410 both do. So a work order naming a reserved path is approved, posted, and labelled, and is only refused one whole stage later at the implementer's prepare job. The plan-reviewer is asked to catch this by eye (plan-reviewer.md:37, 'Does it touch forbidden_paths?'), but that criterion names the config list, which is exactly the incomplete list this planner reasoned from — the reviewer read the same wrong source and passed the plan. The guard itself is correct; it is simply never consulted while a plan is still cheap to change.
fixes.fix: Add a step to sdlc-plan.yml immediately after 'Validate the work order', running `node .sdlc/bin/check-forbidden.mjs --file work-order.json` under the same `if: steps.stop.outputs.stopped != 'true'` guard, so a reserved path refuses the plan at the point where dropping one files[] entry costs nothing. Then widen plan-reviewer.md:37 and planner.md:161 to say the rule set is the framework's reserved paths unioned with config.yml's forbidden_paths plus branch-dependent rules (guards.js reservedRules), not config.yml's list alone — otherwise a reviewer or planner reading only config.yml will keep reaching the same wrong conclusion.
fixes.diagnosis: The plan cannot be built as described. Its files[2] edits .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md, and on a ticket branch the effective rule set reserves the whole of .sdlc/memory/ — not because config.yml lists it, but because reservedRules() appends '.sdlc/memory/**' whenever the head branch is neither sdlc/project-* nor memory/* (src is .sdlc/bin/lib/guards.js:127). The implement stage's prepare job fetched the approved work order and refused it before any code was written, so nothing of the implementation exists and nothing is worth resuming. The planner made a wrong assumption and said so in its own risks[4]: it claimed the file 'is not in forbidden_paths, so the diff gate will allow it'. That reasoning read only the config list; the framework's own reserved rules are unioned on top of it (guards.js:127 RESERVED + cfg.forbidden_paths + branch-dependent rules), so a path can be reserved without appearing in config.yml at all. The plan is otherwise sound and even prescribes the repair: risks[4] states the selectors.md edit 'records a hook, it does not affect behaviour' and is 'safe to drop'. Replan with files[2] removed and the other two edits (src/web/pages.js, src/web/styles.css) and the test file unchanged. Not transient, not a code defect, not a framework bug in the guard — the guard is right and refused exactly what it should. Separately, no stage between the plan and the implementer ever ran that check, which is why a whole council was spent to learn this; that gap is recorded below.
fixes.evidence: failed-run.log:199-202 — 'sdlc: work order touches reserved paths: .sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md (matched .sdlc/memory/**) / A human must approve this.' then exit 1. The red step is 'Refuse work orders that touch forbidden paths' (.github/workflows/sdlc-implement.yml:130, `node .sdlc/bin/check-forbidden.mjs --file work-order.json`), which runs before any implementer work. Reproduced locally against the plan in previous-work-order.json: reservedRules(cfg, '') contains '.sdlc/memory/**', and findForbidden over its four paths returns exactly [{path:'.sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md', rule:'.sdlc/memory/**'}] — the other three paths are clean. config.yml:197 forbidden_paths does not list .sdlc/memory/**, confirming the planner reasoned from the wrong list. failure-packet.json: attempt=1, occurrences=1, prior_signatures=[] — first and only failure on this issue.

fixes.what: The job that produces plan-review.json (reviewer, line 649-651) and the job that consumes it (publish, step at line 799) ask two different questions about whether a verdict exists. The reviewer job runs on `needs.gate.outputs.gate == 'agent' && needs.gate.outputs.stopped != 'true'`; publish's 'Apply the plan review' step runs on `needs.gate.outputs.gate == 'agent'` alone and then hard-fails at apply-plan-review.mjs:22 when loadArtifact's existsSync finds no file. Neither consults needs.reviewer.result, the only signal that says whether the reviewer actually ran, and publish's own job-level if (line 768) re-tests a third variant. So a gate that says 'agent' with a reviewer job that did not run is a hard failure on a missing file rather than a skipped step. Run 36185881820 took that path on the mode=review route (plan job skipped, gate=agent, reviewer=skipped) and died after the plan had already been validated and kept. It is also not explicable by the file as written under a consistent reading of gate's outputs: reviewer evaluated at 20:28:21, the same second gate completed, and saw the gate output as unset, while publish 3s later read the identical expression as 'agent'.
fixes.fix: Make needs.reviewer.result the single source of truth for 'is there a verdict'. Give 'Apply the plan review' the same `if: needs.reviewer.result == 'success'` already used by the two artifact-handling steps above it (lines 789 and 795), so a reviewer that did not run skips the step instead of dying on a missing file, and drop the `needs.gate.outputs.stopped` term from the reviewer job's if so it and publish stop re-deriving the predicate separately. Then, if a skipped reviewer on the agent gate is genuinely never allowed, make publish fail with a named reason ('the gate required a plan review and the reviewer job did not run') rather than a missing-file error from loadArtifact. Add a self-fix test that dispatches sdlc-plan with the plan job skipped and gate=agent and asserts a reviewer job appears — the mode=review path is the only route that reaches the reviewer with no plan job, and it is untested: the last six runs were all plan=success, reviewer=success.
fixes.diagnosis: The plan-reviewer never ran, and publish demanded its verdict anyway. Root-cause's AC revision (work order v4) went out for re-review: plan-strategy.mjs chose mode=review, so the plan job was skipped and the gate validated the ledger's validated_work_order instead. The gate then decided gate=agent (log: 'gate=agent / reason=gates.plan_review_agent is on'), and publish's 'Apply the plan review' step — conditioned only on needs.gate.outputs.gate == 'agent' (sdlc-plan.yml:799) — ran apply-plan-review.mjs, which died at apply-plan-review.mjs:22 on a plain existsSync('plan-review.json') that was false, because the reviewer job that produces that file (sdlc-plan.yml:649-651) was SKIPPED. Nothing wrote the file. The defect is in the workflow, not the plan, the code, or the environment: two places re-derive 'did we get a verdict?' from different predicates — the reviewer job adds '&& needs.gate.outputs.stopped != "true"' at line 651, publish's step does not — and neither asks needs.reviewer.result, the only value that actually says whether the reviewer ran. So any run where the gate says agent but the reviewer job does not run makes publish hard-fail on a missing file. This run is the first in sdlc-plan.yml's history to reach the reviewer with the plan job skipped (mode=review; the last six runs all show plan=success, reviewer=success). The observed skip is also not explicable by the workflow as written under any consistent reading of gate's outputs: reviewer was evaluated at 20:28:21, the same second gate completed, and saw needs.gate.outputs.gate as unset, while publish, evaluated 3s later, compared the same expression equal to 'agent' and needed.gate.outputs.stopped empty enough for its own job-level if at line 768 to pass. That points at needs-outputs propagation at the instant the producing job completed, but whichever side misfired, the structural gap is the same and is the thing to fix. Re-running cannot help: the mode=review path is deterministic, and it would also burn plan attempt 7 of the budget and re-derive root-cause's AC revision, which already survives. NOT transient — nothing about the environment changed. The prior_signatures are unrelated (cd16743b was implement, b703704e was the 16:02 council-wrote-no-artifact failure already escalated), and this is the first occurrence of 237f8d8d. The work itself survived: work order v4 with the root-cause AC-2/AC-8/AC-9 revision is on the ledger (state/20.json validated_work_order version=4, validated_from=root-cause, validated_at 2026-09-25T20:27:22Z), the gate validated it and uploaded plan-validated, and PR #53 is open. Only the verdict bookkeeping failed.

fixes.what: mode=review has no working path. plan-strategy.mjs restores a stashed validated plan and sets mode=review so that 'only validation, the gate and the reviewer run' (its own comment, plan-strategy.mjs:120-125), but the workflow has no condition that schedules the reviewer in that mode: the plan job is skipped (line 140 admits only single|council) and the reviewer job (line 651) is then skipped anyway even though plan-gate wrote gate=agent and needs.gate.outputs.stopped is empty — both halves of its condition are satisfied, and the identical expression on the publish job's 'Apply the plan review' step (line 797) evaluated true in the same run. So the stage's last step asks for a file no job was scheduled to write. The two conditions are also inconsistent with each other: publish accepts reviewer.result == 'skipped' while still requiring gate.outputs.gate == 'agent', which is exactly the state the workflow produces and cannot satisfy. Not the reporter: apply-plan-review.mjs:17-22 refusing an unactable verdict is the intended behaviour, and the verdict file, the plan and the gate are all correct.
fixes.fix: Give the reviewer a condition that cannot be inherited from the plan job's skip. Change it to `needs: [prepare, gate]` with `if: always() && needs.gate.result == 'success' && needs.gate.outputs.stopped != 'true' && needs.gate.outputs.gate == 'agent'` — the explicit always() plus a success() check on the gate removes the implicit success() that currently resolves against the skipped plan job, and it names the one condition that must hold (this plan goes to an agent). Then tighten publish so the two cannot disagree: keep line 767-770 but move the reviewer's absence into the verdict itself, gating 'Apply the plan review' on `needs.gate.outputs.gate == 'agent' && needs.reviewer.result == 'success'`, so a missing reviewer fails the run at the reviewer boundary with the reviewer's own name in the error rather than 20 seconds later in a script that is only reading a verdict. Cover it with a test that asserts, for mode=review, that the reviewer job is scheduled — the gap is that mode=review is a new path and nothing checked that its one necessary job runs. Do not add a fallback that lets publish post an unreviewed plan when gate=agent: that is the exact hole the agent review exists to close.
fixes.diagnosis: The plan stage chose mode=review, and in that mode the workflow never runs the plan reviewer, so publish then fails for want of a verdict. plan-strategy.mjs:126-146 found root-cause's revised work order on the ledger (validated_from=root-cause, validated_at=22:01:16, validated_ac_changes=AC-3/AC-4), restored it as work-order.json and set mode=review. The plan job's condition is `mode == 'single' || mode == 'council'` (.github/workflows/sdlc-plan.yml:140), so the planner was correctly skipped. The gate job still ran plan-gate.mjs (its step is gated on mode != 'resume') and it wrote gate=agent, rejections=0, confidence=87 — plan_review_agent is on in .sdlc/config.yml:173. The reviewer job's own condition, sdlc-plan.yml:651, is `needs.gate.outputs.gate == 'agent' && needs.gate.outputs.stopped != 'true'`, which those outputs satisfy, and the same expression is what let publish's 'Apply the plan review' step run — yet the reviewer job was skipped. That is the defect: no job condition anywhere in the workflow schedules the reviewer in mode=review. publish permits reviewer.result == 'skipped' (sdlc-plan.yml:767-770) but still runs apply-plan-review.mjs when gate.outputs.gate == 'agent', and the copy of plan-review.json is gated on reviewer.result == 'success', so apply-plan-review.mjs:21-22 loadArtifact finds nothing and dies. This is not a bad plan and not a bad run: the plan validated, the gate passed, and the review the stage exists to perform never happened. It is deterministic and has now cost two runs (36185881820 at 20:27 and 36194614924 at 22:01, byte-identical message, both mode=review), so a third dispatch would burn attempt 4 of 10 and change nothing — the stash is still on the ledger, so mode=review is chosen again, the plan job is skipped again and the reviewer is skipped again. Note also that the two reviewer-skipped runs that are healthy (36183731580, 36157875366, 36115257837) all show gate=human, so gate.outputs.gate is read correctly in general; plan=skipped is the only thing that distinguishes the two broken runs, and it is the mode=review path that has never once run a reviewer. I could not pin the exact Actions-level evaluation step that turns a satisfied condition into a skipped job, and I am not going to guess at it in a fix — the observable behaviour and the file that owns it are both unambiguous. What survives and must not be redone: PR #59 is open on sdlc/issue-55 with the implementation already committed (97295e8, 'Close the five holes the review found in the #55 cascade guard', 275 pass / 0 fail), and root-cause's revised work order is stashed on sdlc-state as state/55.json validated_work_order with its AC-3/AC-4 diff, while the ledger's pending block still points at root-cause from the QA run 36192850610. The reviewer this run owed has never been produced and cannot be produced without a fixed workflow, so resume is not available either — there is no stranded step to continue from, only a step that never started.
